problems.title: A product-to-sum constant
problems.question: Solve cos x=a with a=2cos20°cos40°−cos20°.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
steps: a=cos60°+cos20°−cos20°=1/2. Thus x=2kπ±π/3.

problems.title: An identity fixes a frequency
problems.question: Find a for which sin4x(cos⁴2x−sin⁴2x)=sin(ax)/2 for every x.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: cos⁴t−sin⁴t=cos2t and sin t cos t=sin2t/2.
steps: The left side is sin4x cos4x=sin8x/2. Hence sin(ax)=sin8x for all x.
Differentiating at zero, or comparing the small-input limits, gives a=8, which indeed works.

problems.title: Graph a scaled cosine
problems.question: Graph y=3cos2x+1 and find its domain, range and least positive period.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: For A cos(Bx)+D, amplitude=|A| and period=2π/|B|.
steps: The domain is all reals, range 1±3=[−2,4], and period π.
One cycle passes through (0,4),(π/4,1),(π/2,−2),(3π/4,1),(π,4). Join with a smooth cosine curve and repeat.

problems.title: Factor a trigonometric sum
problems.question: Solve cos x+cos2x+cos4x=0.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
steps: The equation becomes cos x(1+2cos3x)=0.
cos x=0 gives x=π/2+kπ. cos3x=−1/2 gives x=2kπ/3±2π/9.

problems.title: Count intersections of a sine and a shallow line
problems.question: How many real x satisfy sin x=x/13? Justify.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Necessarily |x|≤13; the equation is odd-symmetric. On a positive sine lobe, sin x−x/13 is strictly concave.
steps: Zero is a root. On (0,π), the difference starts with positive derivative and ends negative, giving exactly one positive root.
On (2π,3π), the endpoints are negative and the midpoint 5π/2 is positive because 1−5π/26>0. Strict concavity gives exactly two roots.
Negative sine lobes have no positive-x roots. On [4π,13], sin x≤x−4π≤13−4π<4π/13≤x/13, so there are none.
There are three positive roots, three negative partners and zero, totaling seven.

problems.title: Two perpendicular unit vectors in the plane
problems.question: a²+b²=c²+d²=1 and ac+bd=0. Find ab+cd.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: A perpendicular unit vector to (a,b) is either (−b,a) or its negative.
steps: Thus (c,d)=±(−b,a). In either case cd=−ab, so the sum is zero.

problems.title: Three inclined planes through an equilateral triangle
problems.question: Planes through the three triangle sides meet at K and make 60° with the triangle plane. K is height 6√3 above it. Find the triangle inradius.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: If H is K’s projection, its distance to each side line is d=h cot60°=6.
steps: If H lies inside the triangle, it is the incenter and r=6.
The text does not require H inside. It may instead be an excenter. In an equilateral triangle an exradius equals 3r, so d=6 would give r=2.
Both give the same acute 60° plane angles with the stated height.
problems.answer: 6 for an interior projection; 2 is also possible without that restriction.
problems.note: The usual intended projection is inside the triangle. An exterior excenter is not excluded by the stated plane and distance conditions.

problems.title: Project a rhombus onto an inclined plane
problems.question: A parallelogram has diagonals 6,8 and one side 5, and lies on a face of a 60° dihedral angle. Find its orthogonal projection area on the other face plane.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Parallelogram law; rhombus diagonals are perpendicular; projected area=S cos theta.
steps: The other side squared is (36+64)/2−25=25, so it is a rhombus. Its area is 6×8/2=24.
The projected area is 24cos60°=12.

problems.title: Angle between projections of equal oblique segments
problems.question: Two equal oblique segments from a point to a plane make angle alpha with the perpendicular and angle beta with each other. Find angle gamma between their projections.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Decompose each unit direction into normal and planar components.
steps: The common normal component has length cos alpha; each planar component length sin alpha.
The dot product identity is cos beta=cos²alpha+sin²alpha cos gamma. Solve for cos gamma and take arccos.
For nonzero projections, 0<alpha<π/2 and feasibility requires the quotient to lie in [−1,1].

problems.title: Centroid distance needs signs of vertex distances
problems.question: Triangle vertices are distances 5,6,7 from a plane. Find the centroid’s possible distances.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Signed distance of the centroid is one third of the signed-distance sum.
steps: If all vertices are on one side, the distance is (5+6+7)/3=6.
If one is on the opposite side, the possible absolute sums are |−5+6+7|=8,|5−6+7|=6,|5+6−7|=4.
Divide by 3. Reversing all signs adds no new values.
problems.note: The source does not state that the triangle lies entirely on one side of the plane. Without this condition the answer is not uniquely 6.
